svg.text: Failover: claiming a dead executor's buckets (no COMMIT message)
A survivor learns it owns bucket b when its own claim succeeds. Every survivor computes the same HRW split, so no coordination is needed.
t
D's last heartbeat
0 s · D crashes
claim threshold (5 s): D's leases not yet claimable
5 s · claimable
next roster poll
≤ 6 s · detect
claim buckets · resume
~6–8 s · resumed
Step 1 · claim D's buckets
SELECT bucket FROM bcs_task_leases
WHERE node_id = :D -- ~4096/N rows
-- claim those that rank me first without D
a handful of claims per survivor, in milliseconds
next-ranked survivor after a 1 s grace if #1 is down too
then D's node_id is on no lease row:
nothing left to watch
idle sessions: loaded on their next round
Step 2 · resume pending sessions, per bucket
… WHERE bucket = :b AND has_pending_work LIMIT 2000
batch after batch, unprocessed input first; state reloads
lazily; input recorded by the fallback is found here too.
Step 3 · safety-net sweep (30–60 s)
Buckets with a stale owner; pending sessions nobody
drives: catches failed claims, restarting nodes, etc.
Taking over earlier on evidence (fencing makes a wrong guess safe; it only costs a rehydration)
Same advertise_addr, new node_id — the process restarted in place; two processes can't listen on one address → old run's buckets
claimable as soon as the new roster row is seen. RTO ≈ restart time + ≤ 1 s.
Mark own roster row dead on panic — survivors claim its buckets at once; best effort (not on OOM kill / kill -9).
Relative staleness — stale(D) = max(heartbeats) − heartbeat(D), plus a recovery grace: nobody claims until its own heartbeats are healthy for 5 s.
A node that is alive but silently unreachable gives no evidence: wait the claim threshold.
